routes.label: Check the smallest entry in each row

question:
Which number in the array below is both the largest in its column and the smallest in its row? (Columns go up and down, rows go right and left.)

\[\begin{array}{ccccc} 10 & 6 & 4 & 3 & 2 \\ 11 & 7 & 14 & 10 & 8 \\ 8 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 9 \\ 13 & 4 & 15 & 12 & 1 \\ 8 & 2 & 5 & 9 & 3 \end{array}\]
solution:
Any qualifying entry must first be the smallest number in its row. From top to bottom, the row minima are
\[
2,\quad7,\quad3,\quad1,\quad2.
\]
The \(7\) is in the second column, whose entries are \(6,7,3,4,2\). Thus it is also the largest number in its column.

The minima in the first and fourth rows lie in the fifth column, which contains \(9\), so they fail. The minima in the third and fifth rows lie in the second column, which contains \(7\), so they also fail. We have checked every row minimum, so the unique qualifying number is \(\boxed{7}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
